newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Red Cross seeks civilian safety in Sri Lankan war.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross seeks civilian safety in Sri Lankan war.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) on Wednesday appealed to both sides in Sri Lanka's long-running ethnic conflict to spare civilians.

In a statement issued to mark "Red Cross and Red Crescent Day" on May 8, Gerard Peytrignet, head of the ICRC delegation on the Indian Ocean island, called for more respect for humanitarian law in the war.

"The ICRC wishes to call for the absolute necessity to spare the civilian population from the effects of hostilities and to make a clear distinction in the attack, as in the defence, between military and civilian objectives...," he said.

He called on those involved in battle to abide by rules of humanitarian law applicable in armed conflict and emphasised respectful treatment of prisoners captured on the battlefield, along with those who lay down arms or are unfit to fight.
Human rights activists have criticised both government forces and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels for human rights abuses in the conflict, now in its 14th year.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the rebel war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east, but the guerrillas say the toll is higher.
